title: Go SDK: decoding pipeline with generic validators and streaming backpressure
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: Current Go SDK streaming helpers assume complete JSON messages per event and perform ad-hoc unmarshalling. That leaves callers to implement noisy glue for partial JSON chunks, tokenized structured output, and per-message validation. We also lack a composable pattern that combines typed structs with generic validators and backpressure to avoid unbounded memory growth when consumers are slower than the network.

Goal: Build a reusable decoding pipeline that: (1) incrementally assembles partial JSON from the stream, (2) exposes a typed, generic Validate+Decode API for structured output, (3) integrates with a channel-based backpressure mechanism, and (4) composes with an idempotent retry middleware for transient server failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Public API: Decoder[T any]{ Next(ctx) (T, error) } that returns typed T values as they become available from a streaming response.
- Generic validator: Validator[T any] interface + helper generators to derive validators from struct tags for common checks (required, enum, min/max length).
- Streaming robustness: Decoder must gracefully handle partial chunks, recover from truncated JSON between server reconnects (when retrying), and surface clear decoding errors with byte offsets for easier debugging.
- Backpressure: Consumer pace should drive the internal buffer size; default buffer is 64 events, and we expose options to configure capacity and a DropOldest()/BlockOnFull() policy.
- Retry integration: Provide a documented pattern and middleware that retries whole request streams on transient 5xx with exponential backoff and proper idempotency keys, ensuring the decoder can resume or fail fast depending on policy.
- Tests & benchmarks: Unit tests for partial-chunk assembly, validator edge cases, and an integration benchmark that shows <3% median latency regression for common chat workloads compared to current streaming helpers.

Non-goals: full schema language (we defer to proto/jsonschema later), automatic schema migration tooling in this ticket.
comments: 2026-03-03 - LP: Ticket created after spike. Spike found a common failure mode where partial JSON like '{\"id\":1,\"payload\":{\'a\':' was split across two frames and produced an unhelpful error. Proposed a state-machine based incremental parser plus typed generics for validation.

2026-03-05 - MO: Implemented first pass of 'chunkAssembler' + tests for split-object and split-string cases. Using encoding/json's Decoder.Buffered combined with a small state machine for depth counting to know message boundaries. Draft PR opened (WIP).

2026-03-07 - LP: Review notes: prefer composable Decode/Validate separation (Decoder returns raw JSON snippets, Validator[T] does structural checks). Also requested an option to return a streaming 'Envelope' that includes metadata (seq, partial, source) for consumers that need auditability.

2026-03-09 - MO: Changed approach: Decoder now emits 'raw bytes' via NextRaw() used only internally; public Next() calls the generic Unmarshal+Validate pipeline. Added context cancellation handling to unblock blocked consumers. Added options: BufferCapacity (default 64), OverflowPolicy=(block|drop_oldest).

2026-03-10 - QA (R. Chen): Ran fuzzer against chunk boundaries for 5000 iterations, found 2 issues: (1) bufferedDecoder leak when consumer cancels mid-stream, (2) validators panicked on unexpected number fields. Pushed fixes: ensure goroutine cleanup and add recover() around reflection-based validators. Added regression tests.

2026-03-12 - PM (J. Alvarez): Confirmed acceptance criteria with product. Asked for an example showing how to wire retries with idempotency keys and how to handle resumed streams (we plan to add a short doc in examples/).

2026-03-13 - MO: Benchmarks: Microbench harness with synthetic chat stream (avg 256 tokens, 3 messages/response). Compared old helper vs new decoder: median per-message decode latency increased by 1.8% but CPU decreased by ~5% due to avoidance of repeated allocations. Memory under slow consumer scenario decreased 60% with default overflow policy. Added benchmarks to PR.

2026-03-14 - LP: Addressed final review comments, updated public docs, and added a migration note describing how to switch from legacy StreamJSON -> Decoder[T]. Preparing to mark In Review after one more round of API doc proofreading.
